scope: Four safety/lifetime clarifications for isolated, explicitly attributed AI narration. Not a replacement translation, acoustic/source-role approval, installed insertion or closure of any original finding.
comparison_authority: Whole-sentence alternative readings with different wording and punctuation, not a controlled single-variable emotion experiment. Edge-TTS style controls or official phoneme pronunciations are not claimed. No automatic winner or global dictionary update.
primary_reference_authority: Existing kernel documentation and C++ basic.life snapshots are reused unchanged. A newly retrieved C++ memory working-draft snapshot provides the monotonic resource contract. These are independent technical clarifications, not reconstructions of 2019 speech or proof of local policy/runtime.

cases.finding: Ordinary demand-backed anonymous-page placement depends on faulting access, applicable policy and allowed nodes, not solely on the location of malloc. Linux default local/preferred-local allocation can fall back to other allowed nodes. This does not imply the same fallback for explicit bind policies or guarantee locality.
preserved_constraints: ordinary demand-backed anonymous pages
malloc call alone is insufficient
first actual access and applicable policy/allowed nodes matter
default local policy may fall back
not a statement about all bind policies
not a local configuration or locality guarantee
cases.reading_comparison: NUMA/malloc in one full sentence versus their explanatory Chinese descriptions in another. Neither is an approved pronunciation or source-speaker performance.

cases.finding: Linux documents distinct overcommit modes. The general possibility of overcommit does not guarantee malloc success or justify removing its failure handling. A nonnull virtual-allocation result is not a general guarantee of future backing for every touched page. The original negation in unit212 remains unresolved; neither candidate purports to recover it.
preserved_constraints: different policies
no always-success claim
retain malloc null/failure handling
nonnull is not a general future-backing guarantee
no reconstructed source negation or platform guarantee
cases.reading_comparison: Direct malloc identifier versus explanatory Chinese allocation wording, with an additional rhetorical question. Multiple wording/prosody variables differ.

cases.finding: Retaining pool storage does not extend an object lifetime that has ended. Before a valid new lifetime, old pointers have only limited allowed uses; ordinary access to the old object's nonstatic members is not justified by the address remaining allocated. The pool is not by itself a safe-reclamation protocol. These samples do not attempt to resolve every ABA case or the implementation-extension issue in the original finding.
preserved_constraints: storage retention is not lifetime extension
old pointer has limited permitted uses, not all uses forbidden
ordinary old-member access is not justified
new object lifetime rules still apply
pool alone is not a safe-reclamation protocol
ABA and extension subissues stay open
cases.reading_comparison: C++ symbol read by the engine versus the scoped Chinese reading C加加. No global replacement of plus signs or asserted phoneme outcome.

cases.finding: The specific std::pmr::monotonic_buffer_resource do_deallocate has no effects. release returns memory obtained from the upstream resource and resets buffer state; caller-supplied initial storage remains caller-managed. Releasing storage is distinct from invoking needed object destructors/resource cleanup, and outstanding uses must end first. This is a concrete illustration, not a claim that every region API is identical, and does not close the 2002 benchmark or database-name subissues.
preserved_constraints: specific C++ monotonic resource, not every region API
individual do_deallocate has no effects
release returns upstream allocations
external initial buffer remains caller-managed
end outstanding uses before release
needed destruction and cleanup are not supplied by returning raw storage
2002 study and database-name subissues remain open
cases.reading_comparison: P M R / monotonic buffer resource / deallocate / release whole-sentence identifier reading versus the scoped Chinese single/bulk-release explanation. Exact C++ spelling remains displayed; no official pronunciation is claimed.
